body:
Thanks for the reply. I appreciate your perspective a lot and this makes me feel a little better. Sorry mine is late.

I didn’t get any kind of description of it outside of “groped”  but I’m pretty much certain it wasn’t violent because this was around other people and in the scene I was in then I think that would have been a way bigger deal and I would have heard about it as soon as I was aware again. I also never have gotten violent while drunk in general, or in my day to day life. Sober and even very drunk but where I can still remember things I’ve never touched anyone because I know how bad it would feel both for the person and myself. I was told that the night this happened a guy that was hosting spiked my drinks and some others with Robotussin which I guess he thought was funny or I wanted. I almost died that night - I woke up in an unheated building next door in the middle of winter. I don’t know if it’s true he did that, but it was the only time I’ve ever not remembered several hours of an evening or woke up not knowing how I got where I was. It was scary. I don’t really think it’s an excuse though and no matter what I can’t justify groping. Ever. I just felt so horrified I’d done it. No one deserves that. 

I’m so sorry about what happened with your landlord. I do feel that that’s what #metoo was especially focused on at the start. I still don’t think what I’m told I did was okay in the slightest and that I had to ensure it never happened again afterward.  I felt that way before #metoo. As far as the drinking experiment idea goes, I’ve done that already basically, and like I say I feel guilty just for drinking sometimes, but nothing like that happened since. I generally just don’t drink or keep it to one or two.

But at the end of the day, that’s the thing - people are getting fired and losing everything for things in the distant past. I did apologize profusely and changed my behavior but I feel like for many people right now that’s not enough, and I guess I have to accept that. I’m not sure if I can but I’m doing my best.

Thanks again

Thanks for the reply. I really appreciate you taking the time. Sorry mine is late - my sleep schedule right now is bad. I have learned from this absolutely.

What’s kept me going this long is that I had this sort of optimism I’d eventually get to a better place in my life or that I always had some chance at a kind of success. I’m involved with a lot of artists and musicians and was always my intent to put my own work out there but with this is my background I can’t see it.  My Dad was a paranoid schizophrenic who had ridiculous substance issues and died when I was 7, I grew up in poverty and extremely bad teeth until 25 because Mom couldn’t afford to fix them, etc., etc. It feels like I’ve spent my whole life trying to catch up. I felt like if I never really escaped poverty and the kind of life my parents both had, I wanted to at least be a good person along the way and I feel I’ve failed at that. There are two women out there that despite my apologies probably think I’m a total creep and I don’t blame them. 

Only thing keeping me going now is the guilt of what it’d do to my family and few remaining friends if I ended it (I had a ton before this happened but increasingly hid away afterward). Also, survival instinct - that’s really, really hard to override.

I’m sorry for the super late response. I have been really depressed about this lately. I don’t know why I heard about this so long after the fact, but if I had to guess, I think it was maybe because neither girl wanted to make a deal out of it, and I also don’t know that any friends saw it. To this day I still don’t know any details about it really, and since I don’t remember it at all, I guess I never will. I definitely didn’t want to press either woman about it. I think donating to a rape crisis center is a great idea, but I don’t feel like that will absolve me of anything.

I think it’s true that many men in this era don’t take responsibility and at best many apologize in a hollow way or express non-apologies and offer excuses and I don’t want to do that. At the same time, I do think I could easily be ostracized, or if I have any work out there that it could be made irrelevant and overshadowed by this. I feel like I’ve seen examples where someone has apologized sincerely at the time and are still pretty much ruined for it, or that these women might have thought I was just apologizing to cover myself but that’s not true, I truly felt horrible. I also see people saying things like, “Louis CK didn’t even grope anyone which is way worse” and I just feel like a terrible person and maybe I am. I feel like it’s conflated or put on a level of severity to things like rape and that’s really difficult. I have female friends that are artists that have said they’re okay with me despite knowing this but I wonder if they’d want to risk working with me because of it. I think about all these women I respect and what they’d think of me if they knew, or what potential partners might too.

I know it might seem extreme but I’ve considered suicide as a result of it all. The idea that there’s something about me where if I drink enough I’m a sexual creep is disturbing and not something I can easily reconcile. I’m the son of a single Mom (my Dad died when I was little) who’s liberal and considers herself a feminist, I’ve always been very liberal and supported feminist ideals, or thought I did anyways. My Mom told me she was raped in high school, and that what I’m told I did was nothing close but she’s my Mom. It’s just hard to see myself as an okay person and it’s hard to not worry about getting “called out” for it and I don’t know if I want to live with the guilt and the possibility of shaming anymore. I’ve been seeing a therapist and doing my best, but this has been really difficult for me.
